summary: @servicetitan/error-boundary 38.1.4 executes obfuscated payload via Bun runtime at preinstall
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases at a hardcoded version, extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it with the sibling file math_init.js (execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js])). math_init.js is a ~727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated JavaScript payload (obfuscator.io fingerprints: string-array rotator, hex-named identifiers, character-code decode table). Neither setup.mjs nor math_init.js is listed in package.json.files (declared as ["dist","src"]) — they are undeclared blobs at the tarball root wired into the lifecycle hook. The declared purpose of the package is a React error-boundary library, which has no legitimate need for a second language runtime. Fetching an alternate runtime specifically to execute a bundled obfuscated payload outside Node's normal resolution runs attacker-controlled code on every installer's machine on npm install. The declared-files/tarball mismatch is consistent with a hijack or impersonation of the legitimate @servicetitan/error-boundary package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
